text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
POLITICAL FRONT PAGE NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA - Around 1,200 Polish repatriates from Kazakhstan, central Asia, will return to Poland this year, government repatriation bureau official Marek Kurenda said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The Polish Private Equity Funds No. 1 and 2, administered by Enterprise Investors, have bought a tin packaging plant in Gdansk, northern Poland.
The funds will inject $7 million into the plant's modernisation and restructuring, Enterprise Investors deputy president Jacek Sawicki said.
- The PZB shipping firm will launch a new ferry line from Gdansk, northern Poland, to Nyneshamm, southern Sweden, on June 1 this year.
Summer season lines linking Swinoujcie, northwestern Poland, and Roenne, Bornholm, will start by the end of June, PZB said.
- Bank Czestowchowa will put off its public share offer and its stock will be listed on the Warsaw bourse next year, bank board memeber Dariusz Salajewski said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Growing domestic demand may lead to the economy's overheating, Poland's finance minister Marek Belka said.
Wage growth should be curbed to avoid wage cuts in the future, Belka said.
- Poland's liquid gas consumption has quadrupled in the last five years, reaching 18 kg per head in 1996, Polish liquid gas lobbying body (POGP) president Adam Kubiak said.
- Swedish firms have invested a total of $361 million in 30 development schemes in Poland by the end of 1996, the Polish Foreign Investment Agency (PAIZ) said.
- The PZB shipping firm has received an International Standards Organisation ISO-9002 quality certificate awarded by the Polish Shipping Register (PRS).

- The sales of Poland's 15 largest open-air markets reached seven billion zlotys in 1996 and but unlikely to exceed that level this year, a report by the Gdansk Market Economy Research Institute (IBnGR) said.

- The Katowice province authorities in southern Poland are planning to form economic zones of advanced activity in structurally troubled areas to boost development of the small and medium-size business sectors.

- The Hutmen non-ferrous metals products maker plans to shift from German-mark to US-dollar markets since it gets raw material on the London Metals Exchange from suppliers charging in US dollars, Hutmen's president Henryk Orzechowski said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poltex Methane, the German Eurogas subsidiary, will form a joint venture with the PGNiG state-owned oil and gas mining firm to explore oil and gas in southern Poland.
The new company will invest $15 million in the programme in the next three years.
- South Korea's Samsung plans to invest $200 million in the construction of consumer electronics plants in Poland and Hungary, Samsung said.
ZYCIE

- The listed Optimus computer maker is mulling opening a plant in Slovakia to avoid the new customs duties on electronic component imports introduced in Poland this year, a source who declined to be named said.
PARKIET
- The management of listed bank BRE will propose shareholders on May 28 an issue of 4.5 million shares to be bought by Germany's Commerzbank, BRE said.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
